scope: Read-only source and existing/staged vendor-library evidence; no board/session/environment changes.

observations: GskGLDevice owns an in-memory GHashTable gl_programs keyed by shader operation, flags, color states and variation.
gsk_gl_device_use_program looks up that hash, and on miss compiles vertex/fragment shaders and links a new GL program.
The table is released at GskGLDevice finalization. The reviewed GL path contains no file cache or program-binary read/write.
GskGpuCache timeout primarily manages images, glyphs, texture atlases and tiles; it is not evidence of cross-process shader persistence.
gtk.implication: Warm shader reuse within the same device/process is implemented. A new Settings process can still trigger PVR compiler work; GTK GL disk reuse was not established.

observations: libpvr_mesa_wsi contains MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR, MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DISABLE, MESA_SHADER_CACHE_SHOW_STATS and mesa_shader_cache/mesa_shader_cache_sf/mesa_shader_cache_db strings.
libGLESv2_PVR_MESA contains EnableBlobCache and cached-binary support symbols.
The strings establish available code paths only, not the live PVR cache activation, successful callbacks or hits.

recommendation: Keep cache changes outside the current Mutter SBC A/B. Read live user cache directory/env and measure repeated process launches separately before changing flags; do not invent undocumented apphint settings.
